youtube.title: The traffic jam that moves backward
youtube.description:
The cars move forward. The slow patch can move backward.

In a controlled experiment, 22 cars formed stop-and-go traffic on a circular track with no obstruction. Small speed changes can sometimes grow in dense traffic; not every jam starts this way.

Original explanatory animation and experiment reconstruction. Synthetic narration.
Research: Sugiyama et al. (2008), https://doi.org/10.1088/1367-2630/10/3/033001
youtube.firstComment: The cars aren't reversing—the slow region is changing which cars are inside it. Have you reached the end of a jam and found no obvious obstruction?

tiktok.caption: Ever reached the end of a traffic jam and found… nothing? A slow patch can move backward while the cars keep moving forward. Not every jam starts this way.
tiktok.firstComment: It's the pattern that moves backward, not the cars. No obvious obstruction at the end doesn't prove a jam formed spontaneously.

instagram.caption:
The cars move forward. The traffic pattern can move backward.

Twenty-two cars. A circular track. No obstruction—yet stop-and-go traffic formed. This is one way a jam can begin, not an explanation for every jam.

Original explanatory animation; experiment reconstruction; synthetic narration.
instagram.firstComment: Watch the highlighted cars enter and leave: the jam isn't a fixed group of vehicles. Research: Sugiyama et al. (2008), doi:10.1088/1367-2630/10/3/033001.

facebook.title: Why traffic can stop without a blocked road
facebook.caption:
No accident or roadworks were needed in this controlled experiment: 22 cars on a circular track developed stop-and-go traffic.

In dense traffic, small speed changes can sometimes grow. Cars move forward through the slow patch while the congestion pattern moves backward. Accidents and bottlenecks also cause jams.

Original explanatory animation, experiment reconstruction and synthetic narration.
facebook.firstComment: Have you ever wondered why traffic stopped when the road ahead seemed clear? A wave is one possible explanation; an earlier incident or bottleneck can matter too.
